options.systemPromptTemplate: Classify each bank transaction into exactly one of the current Notion categories provided. The category list is authoritative; do not invent or return old labels. Use Income for income, salary, compensation, reimbursements, and transactions formerly grouped under Services. Use Internal only for transfers between the user's own accounts. Use Misc. when the evidence is insufficient. Return only the required JSON.

categories.description: Anything that does not clearly fit another category; use as the safe fallback.
Restaurants, groceries, cafes, takeaway, and food delivery.
Flights, hotels, rail for trips, and travel bookings.
Income, salary, compensation, reimbursements, and transactions intentionally merged from the former Services category.
Doctors, pharmacies, medical, dental, therapy, and health insurance.
Gyms, sports clubs, classes, trainers, and fitness equipment.
Transfers between the user's own accounts or savings pots.
Rent, landlords, utilities, and other household housing costs.
Local transit, fuel, taxi, parking, and commuting.
Software, electronics, digital services, and computing.
Clearly described non-salary compensation or reimbursement.

parameters.content:
# Authorization / renewal

Run this section only for the first connection or when the Enable Banking consent expires or is revoked.

1. Start authorization
2. Create a signed JWT
3. Request a read-only consent link
4. Approve it in N26

The approval redirects back to the Webhook section.

# Phase 1: Callback / initial import

- N26/Enable Banking returns a one-time callback code here.
- The workflow exchanges that code for a session, selects the enabled N26 account, saves the connection details, then fetches the initial 90-day transaction window.

# Weekly sync

Runs every Monday at 06:00 Europe/Berlin.

It reads the saved account ID from the N26 Connection State Data Table, creates a fresh JWT, and fetches the rolling 90-day window. No interactive N26 approval is needed while consent remains valid.

# Shared transaction processing

Both the callback import and weekly import converge here:

- Split the transactions list into individual items
- Remove items already seen in previous executions
- Classify each new transaction
- Send the result to Notion

# Category routing — draft only

The Text Classifier chooses one existing Notion Category. Each output branch passes through a small Set Category node, which preserves the transaction and adds the selected category. Unclear items go to Misc.

This section becomes live only after the draft is tested and published.

# Notion output

Create Notion finance row maps the transaction into My Finances: Biller, Account, Category, Currency, Date, Payment Reference, and signed Total (w/ Tax).

The final IF checks whether the run came from the Webhook. Only callback runs receive an HTTP response; scheduled runs simply finish.

nodes.name: Set Category: Income
nodes.notes: Preserves the N26 transaction and sets the Notion Category to Income.

nodes.name: Daily N26 sync
nodes.notes: Runs the read-only N26 transaction import every Monday at 06:00 Europe/Berlin. It waits for the saved connection from the first approved N26 callback.
